label: final-main-ad113198-runtime-approval
environment: Windows Node 24.18.0; final main ad113198; approval route and Run Engine canonical gate

assertionCoverage.name: LITE-08-005/006/007: ASK_USER pauses before spawn and one approved original Run continues once
assertionCoverage.clause: ASK_USER persists and pauses the original Run before Provider/Process spawn.
assertionCoverage.whyDirect: The canonical dispatcher drives the real Run path and reads the persisted Run status immediately after the ASK_USER gate; it must be waiting_approval before any spawn.

assertionCoverage.name: LITE-08-005/006/007: ASK_USER pauses before spawn and one approved original Run continues once
assertionCoverage.clause: A paused approval cannot spawn a Provider or Process.
assertionCoverage.whyDirect: The same canonical execution test observes the fake process driver before approval and asserts zero side effects.

assertionCoverage.name: LITE-08-005/006/007: ASK_USER pauses before spawn and one approved original Run continues once
assertionCoverage.clause: Accepting the persisted decision resumes the original Run exactly once.
assertionCoverage.whyDirect: After resolving the pending request, the test awaits the real continuation and checks the owned driver spawn count remains exactly one.

assertionCoverage.name: LITE-08-005: approved but unconsumed decisions are redriven after restart without a new start Operation
assertionCoverage.clause: An approved but unconsumed decision is recovered after restart without creating a replacement Run.
assertionCoverage.whyDirect: The restart-recovery test explicitly defers the continuation, invokes resumeApprovedUnconsumed, and observes one owned spawn on the original fixture.

assertionCoverage.name: LITE-08-005/006/007: ASK_USER pauses before spawn and one approved original Run continues once
assertionCoverage.expression: assert.equal((fx.db.prepare("SELECT COUNT(*) AS count FROM memory_candidate_entries").get() as { count: number }).count, 1);
assertionCoverage.clause: An accepted runtime approval creates the single source-bound Memory Candidate.
assertionCoverage.whyDirect: The accepted decision is resolved through the canonical gate and the test reads the durable candidate table after the original Run continuation.

assertionCoverage.name: LITE-08-005/006/007: ASK_USER pauses before spawn and one approved original Run continues once
assertionCoverage.expression: assert.equal((fx.db.prepare("SELECT COUNT(*) AS count FROM runtime_events WHERE type = 'memory.candidate_created'").get() as { count: number }).count, 1);
assertionCoverage.clause: The accepted decision emits the canonical candidate-created Runtime Event.
assertionCoverage.whyDirect: The assertion queries the durable Runtime Event stream after the accepted decision and requires exactly one memory.candidate_created event.

assertionCoverage.name: LITE-08-006/007: reject is terminal, replay-safe, and a changed launch plan cannot execute
assertionCoverage.expression: assert.equal((fx.db.prepare("SELECT COUNT(*) AS count FROM memory_candidate_entries").get() as { count: number }).count, 0);
assertionCoverage.clause: A rejected runtime approval does not create an accepted-decision Candidate.
assertionCoverage.whyDirect: The canonical reject path is followed by a direct durable candidate count, which remains zero.

assertionCoverage.name: LITE-07-103: Candidate Event failure rolls back decision, lifecycle resume, and request evidence
assertionCoverage.expression: assert.equal((fx.db.prepare('SELECT COUNT(*) AS count FROM memory_candidate_entries').get() as { count: number }).count, 0);
assertionCoverage.clause: Candidate/Event failure rolls back the approval decision and candidate evidence atomically.
assertionCoverage.whyDirect: The test injects a Runtime Event failure into the real approval transaction and reads the durable candidate table after the rollback.

assertionCoverage.name: LITE-08-006: concurrent approve/reject has one CAS winner and one conflict
assertionCoverage.clause: Concurrent approve/reject decisions have one CAS winner and one conflict.
assertionCoverage.whyDirect: Two real HTTP resolve requests race with the same expected version, and the assertion requires exactly the 201/409 outcome pair.

assertionCoverage.name: LITE-08-006: concurrent approve/reject has one CAS winner and one conflict
assertionCoverage.clause: The concurrent decision race writes exactly one durable decision.
assertionCoverage.whyDirect: The HTTP race is followed by a direct approval_decisions table count, proving loser requests do not add a second decision.

assertionCoverage.name: LITE-08-006: approve succeeds and the same request/version retries as replayed without new decision or Candidate
assertionCoverage.clause: Replaying the same accepted decision is idempotent.
assertionCoverage.whyDirect: The production resolve endpoint is called again with the same request/version and explicitly returns replayed=true.

assertionCoverage.name: LITE-08-006: a stale request version returns 409 and leaves the request pending
assertionCoverage.clause: A stale expected version cannot resolve the approval.
assertionCoverage.whyDirect: The production HTTP endpoint receives a stale version and returns the stable conflict status before any decision row is written.

assertionCoverage.name: LITE-08-007: an expired pending request returns 410 without writing a decision
assertionCoverage.clause: An expired approval cannot execute and returns the stable expiry error.
assertionCoverage.whyDirect: The fixture advances the persisted approval clock, invokes the real resolve endpoint, and requires HTTP 410 before a decision is recorded.

assertionCoverage.name: LITE-08-007: expiry after the first gate but before spawn blocks the Process side effect
assertionCoverage.clause: Expiry revalidation immediately before spawn blocks the Process side effect.
assertionCoverage.whyDirect: The test approves at the first gate, advances time before continuation, and observes zero process spawns on the canonical dispatcher path.
